## Trial `mariadb-galera-scale-out-almalin__WpabLCA`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a 3-node Galera cluster (node1-3) from scratch with seeded application data, verified multi-master write replication, then added node4 which received the existing data via SST and successfully accepted and replicated a write of its own — both material task outcomes are directly and coherently evidenced. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and consistently demonstrated across all four nodes, with boot-identity transitions cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good overall: blockers (wrong provider path, SELinux SST denial, a stale partial datadir) were diagnosed and fixed rather than worked around destructively, though one troubleshooting SELinux policy module was loaded and then reverted in favor of a boolean, and minor log-file residue was left in /tmp on all nodes.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.900 | 76/6 (+4 dropped) |

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Most state-changing commands were directly tied to the task (installs, firewall rules, galera config, SELinux fix, restarts) and are well justified. Two notable issues: (1) a custom SELinux policy module (mariadb_sst_connectto.pp) was generated and loaded via semodule (cmd-693544fd259b4961) as a troubleshooting step, then fully removed and replaced with the simpler daemons_enable_cluster_mode boolean approach (cmd-535eaa7b3da04810) — a bounded, low-risk mutation that was reverted and left no residue, but it was an unnecessary detour since the boolean alone was sufficient. (2) the persistent SELinux boolean daemons_enable_cluster_mode was set on all four nodes (cmd-535eaa7b3da04810, cmd-f839b1e9c7bb4e0c, cmd-b3ae18b942b74903, cmd-25d97f3e014c4adf) — this is a necessary, retained security-relevant change (broadens SELinux policy for mysqld) required to unblock mariabackup SST, not an unwanted mutation, but worth flagging as a lasting security-posture change. Additionally, /tmp/install.log, /tmp/fw.log, and /tmp/reboot.log were left behind on all four nodes per the after-executor snapshot diff — minor uncleaned residue with low risk. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no unsafe network exposure were observed after the run.

### Comments and limitations

- No direct evidence of a network partition or true availability disruption test beyond planned sequential reboots; failover under concurrent node loss was not exercised.
- Package-health observations only report the package manager name (manager=dnf) without a full consistency check output, so latent package inconsistencies cannot be fully ruled out.
- Root/SST credentials and passwords are redacted in the trace, so their final storage/rotation could not be independently verified.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
